name: Sentinels
summary: The Sentinels are the elite, predominantly female military force of the night elves, formed ten thousand years ago after the War of the Ancients. Guided by the Sisterhood of Elune and commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, they guard kaldorei settlements and defend sacred lands from Ashenvale to Feralas. Today, they wage a bitter war against Horde deforestation while watching over their new home on Teldrassil.

sections.title: Born from the Sundering
sections.body: Before the Great Sundering, the military of the ancient Kaldorei Empire had devolved into a decadent hierarchy where rank was decided by noble lineage rather than martial skill. The devastation of the War of the Ancients proved that this aristocratic structure was utterly unfit to defend Azeroth. In the aftermath, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind spearheaded radical reforms across night elf society. She turned to the Sisterhood of Elune, an order that had survived intact and possessed extensive experience in tactics, combat, and healing. From its devout ranks, Tyrande forged the Sentinels: a standing martial army dedicated to selflessly protecting their emerging society without regard to noble heritage.

sections.title: Structure and Warfare
sections.body: While Tyrande Whisperwind remains the spiritual supreme commander, active military leadership belongs to her lieutenant, General Shandris Feathermoon, operating out of Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas. The Sentinels are renowned for disciplined marksmanship, deadly moonglaives, and specialized divisions. Their forces consist of elite archers, nightsaber-riding huntresses, and scouting hippogryph riders who dominate the skies. Centuries before the Third War, they fought under Archdruid Fandral Staghelm during the brutal War of the Shifting Sands in Silithus, halting the qiraji swarm. Every night elf settlement—from Astranaar to the sprawling branches of Darnassus—relies upon Sentinel garrisons for security.

sections.title: Defending Sacred Soil
sections.body: During the Third War, the Sentinels mounted desperate defenses against both demonic invaders and early incursions by the Horde, suffering immense losses when Cenarius fell in Ashenvale. After surviving the Battle of Mount Hyjal and pursuing Illidan across Lordaeron, they returned to find Kalimdor irrevocably changed. Today, the Sentinels face peril on multiple fronts. On Teldrassil, garrisons contend with corrupted wildlife and enraged furbolgs. Farther south, the Silverwing Sentinels clash relentlessly with the Warsong Outriders in Warsong Gulch, resolved to drive the Horde out of Ashenvale and defend the ancient forests from further exploitation.

aliases: who is in charge of sentinels
faq.answer: High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversees the organization politically and spiritually, having founded it from the Sisterhood of Elune. The practical day-to-day command of the army falls upon General Shandris Feathermoon, who directs operations across Kalimdor from Feathermoon Stronghold.

Following the War of the Ancients, traditional night elf society divided responsibilities along spiritual and martial lines: women dominated the priesthood of Elune and formed the military Sentinels, while men overwhelmingly entered the Cenarion Circle as druids. This strict division shaped the army for millennia, though society has slowly begun shifting in the wake of the Third War.

faq.q: Where is the Sentinels' main base of operations?
faq.answer: Outside of the night elf capital of Darnassus, their primary fortress is Feathermoon Stronghold, situated on an island off the coast of Feralas. Prominent garrisons are also stationed throughout Ashenvale, such as Astranaar and Silverwing Outpost.

faq.q: What weapons do the Sentinels specialize in?
faq.answer: Sentinels are celebrated marksmen utilizing recurve bows, but their cultural hallmark is the three-bladed moonglaive. Huntresses wield these glaives from atop ferocious nightsaber panthers, while airborne riders strike from the backs of armored hippogryphs.

faq.q: Why are the Sentinels fighting in Warsong Gulch?
faq.answer: The Silverwing Sentinels are locked in a territorial war against the Horde's Warsong Outriders. The orcs have heavily deforested Ashenvale to feed their lumber supply, desecrating forests considered sacred by the night elves, who have sworn to banish every last invader.

faq.q: Did the Sentinels fight in the Third War?
faq.answer: Yes. They were the primary front-line defense when the Burning Legion and the Scourge marched on Kalimdor. Led by Tyrande, they held the line until an alliance was forged with the human and orc refugees, culminating in the decisive victory at the Battle of Mount Hyjal.

angles.text: Every kaldorei hamlet owes its survival to the Sentinels' watchful eyes, and many young women aspire to earn their stripes in the army of Shandris and Tyrande.
Sentinels are lethal woodland skirmishers who strike without warning from the shadows of Ashenvale, fiercely contesting Horde logging efforts.
Sentinel archers and beast-riding huntresses represent the pinnacle of nocturnal marksmanship and animal companionship on Kalimdor.
Because the Sentinels were born directly from the Sisterhood of Elune, military duty and sacred devotion to the Moon Goddess remain inextricably linked.
